1|# Muse Code task: Expertery v0, an installable private factory with an exam agent (2026-11-03)
2|
3|Repo: ~/projects/forge. Read README.md first (what Expertery is), then this spec. Build a command-line
4|product `expertery` that a company installs into ITS OWN Modal cloud account (private: its past work, exams and
5|trained model stay in its account). v0 supports one tool: CadQuery CAD.
6|
7|Hard rules
8|- Do NOT change: experiments/brackets/** (frozen), examples/past-work-brackets/** (demo data), experiments/final/
9|  RULE_CARD.md, experiments/first-test/**, results/**, forge-wiki/**, README.md, app/**, deploy/modal_web.py.
10|- You MAY import/reuse (not rewrite) existing modules: experiments/final/cloud_cq.py (run_answer_in_box, the grader
11|  app `forge-cq-grader` and its `grade(exam, job_id, brep_bytes, reference=...)` / `measure_brep`),
12|  experiments/first-test/runner.py (SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_messages("A", text, ""), build_body),
13|  experiments/factory/teacher.py (SPARK_MODEL, SPARK_URL, MAX_TOKENS, TEMPERATURE, TOP_P),
14|  experiments/final/run_final_session.sh and run_base_session.sh, experiments/train/forge_train.py, deploy/modal_forge.py.
15|- No Modal, network or model call while you work. All tests use fakes. Run:
16|  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest expertery -q` and the existing `.venv/bin/python -m pytest experiments/final -q`.
17|- In any zsh/sh you write, always brace variables next to a colon: "${JOBS}:x", never "$JOBS:x" (zsh modifiers).
18|
19|## Layout
20|- `pyproject.toml` at the repo root: name `expertery`, version 0.1.0, requires-python >=3.12, dependency `modal`,
21|  console script `expertery = expertery.cli:main`, package `expertery` only.
22|- `expertery/` package: `cli.py` (argparse, subcommands below), `config.py`, `exam_agent.py`, `cloud.py` (thin
23|  adapters over cloud_cq + session scripts; the repo root is the parent of the package dir; add the needed
24|  experiments dirs to sys.path inside the adapter, never at import time of cli.py), `tests/`.
25|- `install.sh` at the repo root: checks `uv` and `modal` exist, runs `uv tool install --editable "<repo dir>"`, then
26|  prints the next step (`expertery init`). It never asks for or prints secrets.
27|- `docs/INSTALL.md`: install, privacy model (what runs where), each command with an example, honest limits (v0:
28|  CadQuery only; practice-job generation still uses the factory scripts; train/serve need GPU money in the user's
29|  account).
30|
31|## Commands
32|Every command that can spend money takes `--cap-dollars` (required, > 0) and `--dry-run` (prints the plan and the
33|estimated cost, spends nothing). Money: estimate each model call from tokens with the teacher's price constants if
34|present (else a constant in config.py with a comment), stop starting new calls when the next could pass the cap,
35|write spent_estimate to the output.
36|
37|1. `expertery init [--dry-run]`: checks the Modal token works (`modal profile current` via subprocess), checks env
38|   for the reader key (EXPERTERY_READER_KEY, falling back to BASETEN_API_KEY; report present/missing, never print
39|   values), deploys the CAD box + grader into the current Modal account (the same deploy cloud_cq uses; find it in
40|   cloud_cq.py / its docstring), writes `~/.expertery/config.json` (tool "cadquery", reader url/model defaults =
41|   teacher SPARK_URL / SPARK_MODEL, overridable by EXPERTERY_READER_URL / EXPERTERY_READER_MODEL so a company can
42|   point at its own Spark Open or Glimmer server).
43|2. `expertery exam build <past-work-dir> --out <exam-dir> --cap-dollars X [--readers 2] [--workers 4] [--dry-run]`
44|   Past work = one folder per job: `request.txt` + `part.py` (CadQuery code that defines `result`). (`part.step`:
45|   print "not supported in v0" and mark the job SKIPPED.) For each job:
46|   a. Reference check: run part.py in the cloud box (run_answer_in_box); it must build one valid solid. Else status
47|      BROKEN_REFERENCE (with the error).
48|   b. Readers: the reader model (Meta Muse Spark Open) gets ONLY request.txt with the factory prompt
49|      (runner.build_messages("A", text, "") + build_body), `--readers` independent tries; extract the code block
50|      like the existing runner does; run each in the box; grade each against the reference with the cloud grader
51|      (exam "factory", reference = part.py source; 0.2% rule as today).
52|   c. All readers PASS → READY. Any reader fails → one more reader call ("explainer") that sees the request text,
53|      the reference part's measurements (bbox, volume, solids) and each failed reader's measurements or run error,
54|      but NEVER the reference code, and must return JSON {"phrase": ..., "why": ..., "suggested_request": ...}
55|      naming the wording a careful engineer could read two ways. Status FLAGGED with that suggestion. If the reply
56|      is not valid JSON → FLAGGED with suggestion null and the raw text kept.
57|   Outputs in exam-dir: `candidates.jsonl` (id, text, reference, status, reader verdicts, measurements, suggestion),
58|   `calls.jsonl` (every model call with tokens, seconds), `report.md` (one table: job, status, readers passed,
59|   phrase/why; totals; spent_estimate; the line "A FLAGGED job is not a model failure: the wording may be read two
60|   ways. A person decides."). Refuse to overwrite an exam-dir that has `exam.jsonl`.
61|3. `expertery exam review <exam-dir> [--accept-all | --keep-all]`: for each FLAGGED job shows original, phrase, why,
62|   suggestion and asks [a]ccept suggestion / [k]eep original / [d]rop job / [e]dit text (reads one line). Writes the
63|   decision + who/when (`"reviewer": "human"`, ISO time) into candidates.jsonl. --accept-all / --keep-all exist for
64|   scripts and tests (record "reviewer": "flag"). Accepted or edited texts are NOT re-checked automatically; report.md
65|   says "re-run `exam build` on edited jobs to re-check them".
66|4. `expertery exam lock <exam-dir>`: refuses while any FLAGGED job has no decision; writes `exam.jsonl` in the runner
67|   jobs-file format (id, family "past-work", level "unknown", text, reference) for READY + accepted/kept/edited jobs,
68|   and `FREEZE.txt` with the sha256 of exam.jsonl and the date. Refuses if exam.jsonl exists.
69|5. `expertery test --exam <exam.jsonl> --model trained|base --name <model-name> --out <dir> --cap-dollars X
70|   [--loop] [--k 3] [--dry-run]`: trained → run_final_session.sh with FORGE_MODEL_NAME=<name>, `--pilot ""`,
71|   `--run "${EXAM}:<sub>:FT:<k>"`; base → run_base_session.sh with `--run "${EXAM}:<sub>:A:<k>"`; `--loop` sets
72|   RUNNER_EXTRA="--bx-loop" (base + loop also needs FORGE_RULE_CARD; trained + loop must run without it; pass the
73|   env through exactly). After a trained run, redeploy deploy/modal_forge.py with the same FORGE_MODEL_NAME (the
74|   session script stops the app; a live product may depend on it). Prints the summary.json pass rate.
75|6. `expertery serve --name <model-name> [--dry-run]`: deploys deploy/modal_forge.py with FORGE_MODEL_NAME; prints the
76|   URL. (The web page is not part of v0.)
77|7. `expertery train --data <train_records.jsonl> --out <volume-subdir> --cap-dollars X [--dry-run]`: runs
78|   `forge_train.py r5 --data ... --out ... --cap-dollars ...` (the guarded entrypoint; never `modal run ...::train`).
79|   Help text says practice data comes from the factory scripts (experiments/factory, experiments/r5) in v0.
80|8. `expertery status`: config (no secrets), which Expertery apps are deployed in the account (`modal app list`),
81|   latest exam dirs found under the current folder.
82|
83|## Tests (expertery/tests, all offline with fakes)
84|- exam build: READY / FLAGGED / BROKEN_REFERENCE / SKIPPED(step) paths with fake box, grader and reader; explainer
85|  never receives part.py text (assert it is absent from the messages); invalid explainer JSON → FLAGGED, null
86|  suggestion; cap stops new calls; dry-run makes zero calls; refuses an exam-dir with exam.jsonl.
87|- review: accept/keep/drop/edit recorded with reviewer and time; --accept-all.
88|- lock: refuses with undecided FLAGGED; writes runner-format rows that runner_final.load_factory_jobs_file accepts;
89|  FREEZE sha matches; refuses overwrite.
90|- test/serve/train/init: the exact subprocess argv and env built (mock subprocess), including "${...}:" safe specs,
91|  FORGE_RULE_CARD rules, and the redeploy after a trained test; no secret value ever in printed output.
92|- `python -m expertery.cli --help` lists all commands.
93|
94|## Report back
95|Files added/changed, both pytest summary lines, and anything you could not do exactly as written.

1|# Expertery
2|
3|> **Name:** the project was first called "Forge", then "Homegrown" (Nov 2-3), now Expertery. Internal code, cloud apps, file names and the frozen
4|> exam files keep older internal names on purpose, so nothing breaks and the exam evidence stays valid.
5|
6|**Expertery turns a small open model into a private expert on your tool, learning only from answers a referee proved
7|correct.** Proven on CAD: Meta's open Muse Glimmer 30B went from **53% (an earlier session, one try) to 83%** on a hand-made exam with no manual, and to
8|**92%** with a self-check loop, about as good as the best setup (94%) that needs a 5,700-word manual, with 2.7× fewer tokens.
9|Built with Muse Spark Open.
10|
11|**▶ Try it live: https://expertery.vercel.app** (one free live try per visitor; the
12|recorded demo is always there)
13|
14|Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 · Indie track, Push the Frontier · build period Oct 27 - Nov 4.
15|
16|![Expertery factory](docs/video/expertery-factory-diagram.png)
17|
18|Interactive diagram: [`docs/video/expertery-factory.html`](docs/video/expertery-factory.html)
19|
20|## Live demo
21|Describe a part; the trained Glimmer (r5f, served from Modal) writes CadQuery code, a locked Modal sandbox builds it,
22|and the model checks its own measurements and fixes the part (up to 3 rounds, the same loop as the 92% second look).
23|You get a 3D view, the measurements, the code and STEP/STL files.
24|- **The badge is a self-check, not the exam referee:** a visitor's part has no reference answer, so "Self-check PASS"
25|  means it built as one solid and its overall size matches the numbers you typed (±0.5%). Otherwise it says "Built
26|  (size not checked)" or "Checks failed".
27|- **Limits:** $15 total for the whole demo, one free live try per visitor, 600 characters per job. When the money is
28|  used up the page pauses and plays a recorded real run. A cold model takes several minutes to wake up (14 min on the
29|  first start), so the page plays the recorded run meanwhile.
30|- **First real live run (2026-11-02):** L-bracket 80 × 30 × 45 mm with two 6 mm holes → Self-check PASS in 120 s,
31|  volume 27,717 mm³ (exactly base + wall − holes). It is the page's recorded run (`app/web/recorded_run.json`).
32|- Hosting: the page is on Vercel (`expertery.vercel.app`) and calls the Modal backend directly from the
33|  visitor's browser (CORS), so the one-try limit sees each visitor's own address.
34|- Code: page `app/web/`, backend `app/backend/`, Modal app `deploy/modal_web.py`, 106 tests in `app/tests/`. Specs:
35|  `specs/MUSE_PRODUCT_*.md`. Steps: `docs/product/DEPLOY.md`.
36|
37|## The problem
38|Companies want AI that is good at their own tools, but big models are expensive, private designs often may not leave
39|the company, and the usual fix is a long manual pasted into every prompt. Can a small open model learn the skill itself?
40|
41|## How the Expertery factory works
42|1. **Job generator** (built by Muse Code): 2,000 practice CAD jobs in 10 part families, each with a hidden correct part.
43|   100 more jobs are locked away as a secret test.
44|2. **First try:** Glimmer (with a one-page rule card) writes CadQuery code. A locked cloud box runs it, and a strict
45|   **referee** compares the part with the correct one (0.2% volume tolerance). 1,882 right, 118 wrong.
46|3. **Self-fix:** Glimmer sees only its own error or its own part's measurements (never the answer). 42 fixed.
47|4. **Spark tutor:** Muse Spark Open gives one short hint, no code, on the 76 still-unsolved jobs. With the hint,
48|   Glimmer solved 52 of 54.
49|5. **Lessons:** only referee-approved answers, with Glimmer's own reasoning, become lessons (1,742). A guard confirmed
50|   no lesson touches the exam. **Wrong answers never teach.**
51|6. **Training:** LoRA on Glimmer 30B (Modal H200, ~2 h, ~$10). The trained model needs no manual and no card.
52|7. **The Expertery box (the product):** the trained Glimmer writes the part, the box builds and measures it, and
53|   Glimmer fixes crashes or mismatches itself (up to 3 rounds) before delivering a checked part.
54|
55|## The Expertery agent (self-check loop)
56|The Expertery box is an agent: the trained Glimmer acts, observes the real result with a tool, and decides what to do
57|next, without ever seeing the correct answer.
58|```
59|describe a part
60|   ↓
61|Glimmer writes CadQuery code
62|   ↓
63|TOOL: locked cloud box runs the code and measures the part (size, volume, number of solids)
64|   ├─ crash      → Glimmer reads the error and rewrites the code
65|   ├─ built      → Glimmer compares the measurements with every number in the request
66|   │                ├─ matches  → "DONE"
67|   │                └─ mismatch → Glimmer rewrites the code
68|   └─ at most 3 rounds; the last part that built is delivered (and, in the exam, graded)
69|```
70|- Reference-free: the agent only sees its own error messages and its own part's measurements, so it works on real
71|  requests where nobody knows the answer.
72|- Measured: on the exam the loop rescued 12 answers (4 after crashes, 8 after a measurement mismatch) and lifted the
73|  trained model from 83.3% to 92.2% (labelled second look). Mean 2.16 rounds per part.
74|- Code: `do_bx_cloud_call` with `--bx-loop` in [`experiments/final/runner_final.py`](experiments/final/runner_final.py).
75|
76|## Results (rules written down before every test; the exam ran once, plus one labelled second look)
77|**Exam: 30 hand-made CAD parts** (15 medium, 15 hard), written before any training and never used to build anything;
78|3 tries each, scored at 0.2%. Plan: [`experiments/final/PLAN.md`](experiments/final/PLAN.md); freeze:
79|[`results/exam-2026-11-02/FREEZE.txt`](results/exam-2026-11-02/FREEZE.txt).
80|
81|| Setup | Score | Hard | Tokens per correct part |
82||---|---|---|---|
83|| Plain Glimmer, short prompt (Oct 28, 1 try, earlier session) | 53% | | |
84|| **Expertery Glimmer, one try (official exam)** | **83.3%** | 73% | 3,352 |
85|| Plain Glimmer + rule card | 85.6% | 84% | 4,145 |
86|| Plain Glimmer + 5,700-word manual, one try (B2) | 87.8% | 76% | 10,662 |
87|| **Expertery Glimmer + self-check loop (second look)** | **92.2%** | 91% | 7,946 |
88|| Plain Glimmer + manual + the same loop (best setup, BX) | 94.4% | 91% | 21,823 |
89|
90|- Expertery + loop vs best setup: **−2.2 points, 95% CI [−11.1, +5.6]**: about as good (pre-registered bar), with no
91|  manual and 2.7× fewer tokens; not faster per answer (266 s vs 301 s).
92|- Expertery one try vs rule card: −2.2 [−12.2, +6.7], a tie. The loop added +8.9 [+1.1, +18.9] points (the loop also
93|  uses "xhigh" reasoning, so both changes are counted together).
94|- **What did not hold:** the original pre-registered claim ("as good as the best setup on one try" and "clearly beats the
95|  manual") **failed**: −11.1 [−24.4, +1.1] and −4.4 [−21.1, +11.1]. The cost bars passed on the token form only.
96|  The 92% is a labelled second look at the same exam, run once with rules written first.
97|- Secret practice-style test (100 jobs from the generator, never trained on): plain 62, plain + card 96, Expertery 96.
98|  The hand-made exam is the harder and more reliable test.
99|
100|Readings: [`results/exam-2026-11-02/`](results/exam-2026-11-02/) (`compare_bars.json`, `compare_ft_acard.json`) and
101|[`results/exam2-ftx-2026-11-02/compare_ftx.json`](results/exam2-ftx-2026-11-02/compare_ftx.json). Every claim with its
102|source: [`forge-wiki/wiki/status.md`](forge-wiki/wiki/status.md).
103|
104|## What we learned (each from a measured failure)
105|- **Study the student before teaching it.** We first ran the untrained Glimmer to see where it fails: in the first
106|  practice run 28 of its 47 crashes came from one CadQuery call that does not exist, so two lines added to its rule
107|  card took it from 74.5% to 94% on the same 200 practice jobs. After that, every lesson started from Glimmer's own
108|  work: its own checked answers and reasoning, self-fix from its own errors, and Spark hints only on the jobs it could
109|  not solve. The training fits how Glimmer works instead of a generic dataset; lessons written in a bigger model's
110|  style made it worse (next point).
111|- Training on a bigger model's answers made Glimmer worse (38%, then 48% vs 52% untrained). Training on its **own**
112|  referee-checked answers worked (62 → 96 on the secret practice test).
113|- The referee is everything: the model learns exactly what the referee approves.
114|- A self-check loop (run, measure, fix) adds about 9 points on hard parts: crashes and two-piece parts get fixed.
115|- A test made by the same generator as the lessons is too easy (96%); the hand-made exam (83%) is the number to trust.
116|
117|## For other tools
118|Only three pieces change per tool: a **job generator**, a **sandbox** to run answers, and a **referee** that decides
119|right or wrong automatically. The rest (Glimmer, Spark tutor, self-fix, lessons, training, the box loop) stays the
120|same. Best exam for a company: 30-100 of its own past jobs with known correct results, never shown to the factory.
121|Status: proven on CAD only.
122|

3|> **Name:** the project was first called "Forge", then "Homegrown" (Nov 2-3), now Expertery. Internal code, cloud apps, file names and the frozen
4|> exam files keep older internal names on purpose, so nothing breaks and the exam evidence stays valid.
5|
6|**Expertery turns a small open model into a private expert on your tool, learning only from answers a referee proved
7|correct.** Proven on CAD: Meta's open Muse Glimmer 30B went from **53% (an earlier session, one try) to 83%** on a hand-made exam with no manual, and to
8|**92%** with a self-check loop, about as good as the best setup (94%) that needs a 5,700-word manual, with 2.7× fewer tokens.
9|Built with Muse Spark Open.
10|
11|**▶ Try it live: https://expertery.vercel.app** (one free live try per visitor; the
12|recorded demo is always there)
13|
14|Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 · Indie track, Push the Frontier · build period Oct 27 - Nov 4.
15|
16|![Expertery factory](docs/video/expertery-factory-diagram.png)
17|

20|## Live demo
21|Describe a part; the trained Glimmer (r5f, served from Modal) writes CadQuery code, a locked Modal sandbox builds it,
22|and the model checks its own measurements and fixes the part (up to 3 rounds, the same loop as the 92% second look).
23|You get a 3D view, the measurements, the code and STEP/STL files.
24|- **The badge is a self-check, not the exam referee:** a visitor's part has no reference answer, so "Self-check PASS"
25|  means it built as one solid and its overall size matches the numbers you typed (±0.5%). Otherwise it says "Built
26|  (size not checked)" or "Checks failed".
27|- **Limits:** $15 total for the whole demo, one free live try per visitor, 600 characters per job. When the money is
28|  used up the page pauses and plays a recorded real run. A cold model takes several minutes to wake up (14 min on the
29|  first start), so the page plays the recorded run meanwhile.
30|- **First real live run (2026-11-02):** L-bracket 80 × 30 × 45 mm with two 6 mm holes → Self-check PASS in 120 s,
31|  volume 27,717 mm³ (exactly base + wall − holes). It is the page's recorded run (`app/web/recorded_run.json`).
32|- Hosting: the page is on Vercel (`expertery.vercel.app`) and calls the Modal backend directly from the
33|  visitor's browser (CORS), so the one-try limit sees each visitor's own address.
34|- Code: page `app/web/`, backend `app/backend/`, Modal app `deploy/modal_web.py`, 106 tests in `app/tests/`. Specs:
35|  `specs/MUSE_PRODUCT_*.md`. Steps: `docs/product/DEPLOY.md`.
36|
37|## The problem
38|Companies want AI that is good at their own tools, but big models are expensive, private designs often may not leave
39|the company, and the usual fix is a long manual pasted into every prompt. Can a small open model learn the skill itself?
40|
41|## How the Expertery factory works
42|1. **Job generator** (built by Muse Code): 2,000 practice CAD jobs in 10 part families, each with a hidden correct part.
43|   100 more jobs are locked away as a secret test.
44|2. **First try:** Glimmer (with a one-page rule card) writes CadQuery code. A locked cloud box runs it, and a strict
45|   **referee** compares the part with the correct one (0.2% volume tolerance). 1,882 right, 118 wrong.
46|3. **Self-fix:** Glimmer sees only its own error or its own part's measurements (never the answer). 42 fixed.
47|4. **Spark tutor:** Muse Spark Open gives one short hint, no code, on the 76 still-unsolved jobs. With the hint,
48|   Glimmer solved 52 of 54.
49|5. **Lessons:** only referee-approved answers, with Glimmer's own reasoning, become lessons (1,742). A guard confirmed
50|   no lesson touches the exam. **Wrong answers never teach.**
51|6. **Training:** LoRA on Glimmer 30B (Modal H200, ~2 h, ~$10). The trained model needs no manual and no card.
52|7. **The Expertery box (the product):** the trained Glimmer writes the part, the box builds and measures it, and
53|   Glimmer fixes crashes or mismatches itself (up to 3 rounds) before delivering a checked part.
54|
55|## The Expertery agent (self-check loop)
56|The Expertery box is an agent: the trained Glimmer acts, observes the real result with a tool, and decides what to do
57|next, without ever seeing the correct answer.
58|```
59|describe a part
60|   ↓
61|Glimmer writes CadQuery code
62|   ↓
63|TOOL: locked cloud box runs the code and measures the part (size, volume, number of solids)
64|   ├─ crash      → Glimmer reads the error and rewrites the code
65|   ├─ built      → Glimmer compares the measurements with every number in the request
66|   │                ├─ matches  → "DONE"
67|   │                └─ mismatch → Glimmer rewrites the code
68|   └─ at most 3 rounds; the last part that built is delivered (and, in the exam, graded)
69|```
70|- Reference-free: the agent only sees its own error messages and its own part's measurements, so it works on real
71|  requests where nobody knows the answer.
72|- Measured: on the exam the loop rescued 12 answers (4 after crashes, 8 after a measurement mismatch) and lifted the
73|  trained model from 83.3% to 92.2% (labelled second look). Mean 2.16 rounds per part.
74|- Code: `do_bx_cloud_call` with `--bx-loop` in [`experiments/final/runner_final.py`](experiments/final/runner_final.py).
75|
76|## Results (rules written down before every test; the exam ran once, plus one labelled second look)
77|**Exam: 30 hand-made CAD parts** (15 medium, 15 hard), written before any training and never used to build anything;
78|3 tries each, scored at 0.2%. Plan: [`experiments/final/PLAN.md`](experiments/final/PLAN.md); freeze:
79|[`results/exam-2026-11-02/FREEZE.txt`](results/exam-2026-11-02/FREEZE.txt).
80|
81|| Setup | Score | Hard | Tokens per correct part |
82||---|---|---|---|
83|| Plain Glimmer, short prompt (Oct 28, 1 try, earlier session) | 53% | | |
84|| **Expertery Glimmer, one try (official exam)** | **83.3%** | 73% | 3,352 |
85|| Plain Glimmer + rule card | 85.6% | 84% | 4,145 |
86|| Plain Glimmer + 5,700-word manual, one try (B2) | 87.8% | 76% | 10,662 |
87|| **Expertery Glimmer + self-check loop (second look)** | **92.2%** | 91% | 7,946 |
88|| Plain Glimmer + manual + the same loop (best setup, BX) | 94.4% | 91% | 21,823 |
89|
90|- Expertery + loop vs best setup: **−2.2 points, 95% CI [−11.1, +5.6]**: about as good (pre-registered bar), with no
91|  manual and 2.7× fewer tokens; not faster per answer (266 s vs 301 s).
92|- Expertery one try vs rule card: −2.2 [−12.2, +6.7], a tie. The loop added +8.9 [+1.1, +18.9] points (the loop also
93|  uses "xhigh" reasoning, so both changes are counted together).
94|- **What did not hold:** the original pre-registered claim ("as good as the best setup on one try" and "clearly beats the
95|  manual") **failed**: −11.1 [−24.4, +1.1] and −4.4 [−21.1, +11.1]. The cost bars passed on the token form only.
96|  The 92% is a labelled second look at the same exam, run once with rules written first.
97|- Secret practice-style test (100 jobs from the generator, never trained on): plain 62, plain + card 96, Expertery 96.
98|  The hand-made exam is the harder and more reliable test.

104|## What we learned (each from a measured failure)
105|- **Study the student before teaching it.** We first ran the untrained Glimmer to see where it fails: in the first
106|  practice run 28 of its 47 crashes came from one CadQuery call that does not exist, so two lines added to its rule
107|  card took it from 74.5% to 94% on the same 200 practice jobs. After that, every lesson started from Glimmer's own
108|  work: its own checked answers and reasoning, self-fix from its own errors, and Spark hints only on the jobs it could
109|  not solve. The training fits how Glimmer works instead of a generic dataset; lessons written in a bigger model's
110|  style made it worse (next point).
111|- Training on a bigger model's answers made Glimmer worse (38%, then 48% vs 52% untrained). Training on its **own**
112|  referee-checked answers worked (62 → 96 on the secret practice test).
113|- The referee is everything: the model learns exactly what the referee approves.
114|- A self-check loop (run, measure, fix) adds about 9 points on hard parts: crashes and two-piece parts get fixed.
115|- A test made by the same generator as the lessons is too easy (96%); the hand-made exam (83%) is the number to trust.
116|
117|## For other tools
118|Only three pieces change per tool: a **job generator**, a **sandbox** to run answers, and a **referee** that decides
119|right or wrong automatically. The rest (Glimmer, Spark tutor, self-fix, lessons, training, the box loop) stays the
120|same. Best exam for a company: 30-100 of its own past jobs with known correct results, never shown to the factory.
121|Status: proven on CAD only.

228|## Run it
229|Needs macOS or Linux, Python 3.12, and for cloud steps a Modal account (and Baseten for the teacher).
230|```bash
231|git clone https://github.com/alyssaaa11/expertery.git expertery && cd expertery
232|python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install cadquery==2.8.0 cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1 modal==1.6.3 pytest
233|.venv/bin/python -I scripts/check_cadquery.py          # expect: size mm 20.0 20.0 20.0, volume 7607.3
234|.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/factory experiments/freecad experiments/train experiments/common
235|.venv/bin/python experiments/factory/make_jobs.py      # 200 jobs + the self-check table, offline
236|.venv/bin/python experiments/factory/gallery.py --out results/factory-gallery   # pictures of 10 parts
237|```
238|Cloud steps (cost money, need `modal setup` and your own keys in environment variables `BASETEN_KEY`,
239|`META_HERDSHOT_API_KEY`, `GLIMMER_URL`/`GLIMMER_KEY`; our `*_session.sh` wrappers read them from envsave): `experiments/final/cloud_cq.py --check-refs --exam factory`
240|(Modal CPU, cents), `experiments/factory/teacher.py --ids pilot --out <dir> --budget-dollars 1.2` (Baseten).

Read text file `specs/MUSE_INSTALLER_2026-11-03.md`.
1|# Muse Code task: Expertery v0, an installable private factory with an exam agent (2026-11-03)
2|
3|Repo: ~/projects/forge. Read README.md first (what Expertery is), then this spec. Build a command-line
4|product `expertery` that a company installs into ITS OWN Modal cloud account (private: its past work, exams and
5|trained model stay in its account). v0 supports one tool: CadQuery CAD.
6|
7|Hard rules
8|- Do NOT change: experiments/brackets/** (frozen), examples/past-work-brackets/** (demo data), experiments/final/
9|  RULE_CARD.md, experiments/first-test/**, results/**, forge-wiki/**, README.md, app/**, deploy/modal_web.py.
10|- You MAY import/reuse (not rewrite) existing modules: experiments/final/cloud_cq.py (run_answer_in_box, the grader
11|  app `forge-cq-grader` and its `grade(exam, job_id, brep_bytes, reference=...)` / `measure_brep`),
12|  experiments/first-test/runner.py (SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_messages("A", text, ""), build_body),
13|  experiments/factory/teacher.py (SPARK_MODEL, SPARK_URL, MAX_TOKENS, TEMPERATURE, TOP_P),
14|  experiments/final/run_final_session.sh and run_base_session.sh, experiments/train/forge_train.py, deploy/modal_forge.py.
15|- No Modal, network or model call while you work. All tests use fakes. Run:
16|  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest expertery -q` and the existing `.venv/bin/python -m pytest experiments/final -q`.
17|- In any zsh/sh you write, always brace variables next to a colon: "${JOBS}:x", never "$JOBS:x" (zsh modifiers).
18|
19|## Layout
20|- `pyproject.toml` at the repo root: name `expertery`, version 0.1.0, requires-python >=3.12, dependency `modal`,
21|  console script `expertery = expertery.cli:main`, package `expertery` only.
22|- `expertery/` package: `cli.py` (argparse, subcommands below), `config.py`, `exam_agent.py`, `cloud.py` (thin
23|  adapters over cloud_cq + session scripts; the repo root is the parent of the package dir; add the needed
24|  experiments dirs to sys.path inside the adapter, never at import time of cli.py), `tests/`.
25|- `install.sh` at the repo root: checks `uv` and `modal` exist, runs `uv tool install --editable "<repo dir>"`, then
26|  prints the next step (`expertery init`). It never asks for or prints secrets.
27|- `docs/INSTALL.md`: install, privacy model (what runs where), each command with an example, honest limits (v0:
28|  CadQuery only; practice-job generation still uses the factory scripts; train/serve need GPU money in the user's
29|  account).
30|
31|## Commands
32|Every command that can spend money takes `--cap-dollars` (required, > 0) and `--dry-run` (prints the plan and the
33|estimated cost, spends nothing). Money: estimate each model call from tokens with the teacher's price constants if
34|present (else a constant in config.py with a comment), stop starting new calls when the next could pass the cap,
35|write spent_estimate to the output.
36|
37|1. `expertery init [--dry-run]`: checks the Modal token works (`modal profile current` via subprocess), checks env
38|   for the reader key (EXPERTERY_READER_KEY, falling back to BASETEN_API_KEY; report present/missing, never print
39|   values), deploys the CAD box + grader into the current Modal account (the same deploy cloud_cq uses; find it in
40|   cloud_cq.py / its docstring), writes `~/.expertery/config.json` (tool "cadquery", reader url/model defaults =
41|   teacher SPARK_URL / SPARK_MODEL, overridable by EXPERTERY_READER_URL / EXPERTERY_READER_MODEL so a company can
42|   point at its own Spark Open or Glimmer server).
43|2. `expertery exam build <past-work-dir> --out <exam-dir> --cap-dollars X [--readers 2] [--workers 4] [--dry-run]`
44|   Past work = one folder per job: `request.txt` + `part.py` (CadQuery code that defines `result`). (`part.step`:
45|   print "not supported in v0" and mark the job SKIPPED.) For each job:
46|   a. Reference check: run part.py in the cloud box (run_answer_in_box); it must build one valid solid. Else status
47|      BROKEN_REFERENCE (with the error).
48|   b. Readers: the reader model (Meta Muse Spark Open) gets ONLY request.txt with the factory prompt
49|      (runner.build_messages("A", text, "") + build_body), `--readers` independent tries; extract the code block
50|      like the existing runner does; run each in the box; grade each against the reference with the cloud grader
51|      (exam "factory", reference = part.py source; 0.2% rule as today).
52|   c. All readers PASS → READY. Any reader fails → one more reader call ("explainer") that sees the request text,
53|      the reference part's measurements (bbox, volume, solids) and each failed reader's measurements or run error,
54|      but NEVER the reference code, and must return JSON {"phrase": ..., "why": ..., "suggested_request": ...}
55|      naming the wording a careful engineer could read two ways. Status FLAGGED with that suggestion. If the reply
56|      is not valid JSON → FLAGGED with suggestion null and the raw text kept.
57|   Outputs in exam-dir: `candidates.jsonl` (id, text, reference, status, reader verdicts, measurements, suggestion),
58|   `calls.jsonl` (every model call with tokens, seconds), `report.md` (one table: job, status, readers passed,
59|   phrase/why; totals; spent_estimate; the line "A FLAGGED job is not a model failure: the wording may be read two
60|   ways. A person decides."). Refuse to overwrite an exam-dir that has `exam.jsonl`.
61|3. `expertery exam review <exam-dir> [--accept-all | --keep-all]`: for each FLAGGED job shows original, phrase, why,
62|   suggestion and asks [a]ccept suggestion / [k]eep original / [d]rop job / [e]dit text (reads one line). Writes the
63|   decision + who/when (`"reviewer": "human"`, ISO time) into candidates.jsonl. --accept-all / --keep-all exist for
64|   scripts and tests (record "reviewer": "flag"). Accepted or edited texts are NOT re-checked automatically; report.md
65|   says "re-run `exam build` on edited jobs to re-check them".
66|4. `expertery exam lock <exam-dir>`: refuses while any FLAGGED job has no decision; writes `exam.jsonl` in the runner
67|   jobs-file format (id, family "past-work", level "unknown", text, reference) for READY + accepted/kept/edited jobs,
68|   and `FREEZE.txt` with the sha256 of exam.jsonl and the date. Refuses if exam.jsonl exists.
69|5. `expertery test --exam <exam.jsonl> --model trained|base --name <model-name> --out <dir> --cap-dollars X
70|   [--loop] [--k 3] [--dry-run]`: trained → run_final_session.sh with FORGE_MODEL_NAME=<name>, `--pilot ""`,
71|   `--run "${EXAM}:<sub>:FT:<k>"`; base → run_base_session.sh with `--run "${EXAM}:<sub>:A:<k>"`; `--loop` sets
72|   RUNNER_EXTRA="--bx-loop" (base + loop also needs FORGE_RULE_CARD; trained + loop must run without it; pass the
73|   env through exactly). After a trained run, redeploy deploy/modal_forge.py with the same FORGE_MODEL_NAME (the
74|   session script stops the app; a live product may depend on it). Prints the summary.json pass rate.
75|6. `expertery serve --name <model-name> [--dry-run]`: deploys deploy/modal_forge.py with FORGE_MODEL_NAME; prints the
76|   URL. (The web page is not part of v0.)
77|7. `expertery train --data <train_records.jsonl> --out <volume-subdir> --cap-dollars X [--dry-run]`: runs
78|   `forge_train.py r5 --data ... --out ... --cap-dollars ...` (the guarded entrypoint; never `modal run ...::train`).
79|   Help text says practice data comes from the factory scripts (experiments/factory, experiments/r5) in v0.
80|8. `expertery status`: config (no secrets), which Expertery apps are deployed in the account (`modal app list`),
81|   latest exam dirs found under the current folder.
82|
83|## Tests (expertery/tests, all offline with fakes)
84|- exam build: READY / FLAGGED / BROKEN_REFERENCE / SKIPPED(step) paths with fake box, grader and reader; explainer
85|  never receives part.py text (assert it is absent from the messages); invalid explainer JSON → FLAGGED, null
86|  suggestion; cap stops new calls; dry-run makes zero calls; refuses an exam-dir with exam.jsonl.
87|- review: accept/keep/drop/edit recorded with reviewer and time; --accept-all.
88|- lock: refuses with undecided FLAGGED; writes runner-format rows that runner_final.load_factory_jobs_file accepts;
89|  FREEZE sha matches; refuses overwrite.
90|- test/serve/train/init: the exact subprocess argv and env built (mock subprocess), including "${...}:" safe specs,
91|  FORGE_RULE_CARD rules, and the redeploy after a trained test; no secret value ever in printed output.
92|- `python -m expertery.cli --help` lists all commands.
93|
94|## Report back
95|Files added/changed, both pytest summary lines, and anything you could not do exactly as written.

231|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):

231|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):
232|    """PASS iff every check holds and the mismatch fraction is within tol.

235|    ...); `mismatch`: answer-XOR-reference fraction of reference volume

381|    as answers: Workplane gives its solid). Needs cadquery.

337|def pgid_rss_kb(pgid):
338|    """Sum RSS (KiB) of all processes in process group `pgid`, via ps."""
339|    try:

31|output) with an in-flight reserve of 8 x $0.35.

def load_factory_jobs_file(path):
    """Dev jobs file (id, family, text, reference): {id, text, family}."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        jobs = [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
    out = []
    for job in jobs:
        if not job.get("id") or not job.get("text"):
            raise ValueError("jobs file %r has a record without id/text"
                             % (path,))
        row = {"id": job["id"], "text": job["text"],
               "family": job.get("family")}
        # Claude small fix (2026-10-31, verifier B7): keep the reference for
        # GRADING only (grade_fn_for); prompts use job["text"] only.
        if job.get("reference"):
            row["reference"] = job["reference"]
        out.append(row)
    return out


def _real_post_fn(endpoint_to_key):
    """POST one chat-completions body with urllib (stdlib only)."""
    def _post(endpoint_arg, body_arg, timeout_arg):
        endpoint_url, key = endpoint_to_key(endpoint_arg)
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            endpoint_arg,
            data=json.dumps(body_arg).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Authorization": "Bearer " + key,
            },
            method="POST",
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_arg) as resp:
            return json.load(resp)
    return _post

## Report: Expertery v0 installer (spec `specs/MUSE_INSTALLER_2026-11-03.md`)

Built exactly what the spec says. No Modal, network, or model calls were made; only the two pytest commands the spec gives were run.

**Files added** (nothing on the Do-NOT-change list touched):
- [`pyproject.toml`](~/projects/forge/pyproject.toml) — name `expertery`, 0.1.0, ≥3.12, `modal` dep, `expertery = expertery.cli:main`, package `expertery` only.
- [`expertery/config.py`](~/projects/forge/expertery/config.py), [`expertery/cloud.py`](~/projects/forge/expertery/cloud.py) — thin adapters reusing `cloud_cq` (box + `factory_grade_fn` wiring as in `runner_final.grade_fn_for`), `runner` (`build_messages("A",…)` / `build_body` / `extract_code`), `teacher` (SPARK_URL/MODEL, prices, in-flight reserve); `sys.path` edits happen inside adapter functions, never at `cli.py` import.
- [`expertery/exam_agent.py`](~/projects/forge/expertery/exam_agent.py) — build (READY / FLAGGED / BROKEN_REFERENCE / SKIPPED; explainer sees measurements only, never reference code; invalid explainer JSON → FLAGGED/null/raw kept; cap stops new calls; dry-run makes zero calls and writes nothing; refuses locked exam-dirs), review (`[a]/[k]/[d]/[e]`, `--accept-all`/`--keep-all` with reviewer `"flag"`, decisions with reviewer + ISO time, re-check line in `report.md`), lock (refuses undecided/unfinished, writes `exam.jsonl` + `FREEZE.txt`, refuses overwrite).
- [`expertery/cli.py`](~/projects/forge/expertery/cli.py) — all 8 commands with `--cap-dollars` (>0, exit 2 otherwise) + `--dry-run` on money commands; `test` builds the exact session-script argv (`--pilot ""`, `"${EXAM}:<sub>:FT|A>:<k>"`), sets `RUNNER_EXTRA="--bx-loop"` for `--loop` (+ `FORGE_RULE_CARD` for base+loop, removed for trained+loop), redeploys `modal_forge.py` after trained runs, prints the `summary.json` pass rate; `serve` prints the URL; `status` shows config without secrets, `modal app list`, latest exam dirs.
- [`install.sh`](~/projects/forge/install.sh), [`docs/INSTALL.md`](~/projects/forge/docs/INSTALL.md), [`expertery/tests/`](~/projects/forge/expertery/tests) (25 tests, all fakes).

** pytest summary lines:**
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest expertery -q` → **25 passed**
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest experiments/final -q` → **77 passed**

**Could not do exactly as written (2 items):**
1. `train` runs `forge_train.py full-r5 …`, not `forge_train.py r5 …` — `r5` is not a real subcommand (argparse would exit 2); `full-r5` is the actual guarded entrypoint (never `modal run …::train`).
2. Added one status, `DEFERRED`, for jobs left without a verdict when the cap stops new calls (the spec defines no status for this case). `lock` refuses while any remain; totals/`report.md`/`docs/INSTALL.md` document it.
